subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE D&T simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Which list correctly names the four types of motion?
questions.explain: The four recognised types of motion are linear, rotary, reciprocating and oscillating.

questions.q: A piston in a car engine moving up and down in a straight line shows which type of motion?
questions.explain: Reciprocating motion is repeated straight-line movement backwards and forwards or up and down, exactly like an engine piston.

questions.q: A metronome arm ticking from side to side about a pivot shows which type of motion?
questions.explain: Oscillating motion swings backwards and forwards along a curved path about a fixed pivot, like a metronome arm or pendulum.

questions.q: Movement in a complete circle around a fixed axis is called...
questions.explain: Rotary motion is continuous turning around a central axis, such as a wheel or a motor shaft.

questions.q: In a first-class lever, the fulcrum is...
options: Between the load and one end only
At the same point as the load
Between the effort and the load
questions.explain: A first-class lever has the fulcrum between the effort and the load, e.g. a see-saw, crowbar or scissors.

questions.q: A nutcracker and a wheelbarrow both have the load between the fulcrum and the effort. What class of lever are they?
questions.explain: A second-class lever has the load between the fulcrum and the effort, giving a mechanical advantage that multiplies the effort force.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a linkage?
options: To transfer or change the direction of motion or force between parts
questions.explain: Linkages are rigid bars joined at pivots used to transfer movement and force and to change their direction or size.

questions.q: A reverse-motion linkage causes the output to...
options: Move in the same direction as the input
Move in the opposite direction to the input
questions.explain: A reverse-motion linkage pivots about a central fixed point so the output moves in the opposite direction to the input.

questions.q: A bell-crank linkage is chosen when a designer needs to...
options: Turn rotary motion into rotary motion
Change the direction of a force through about 90 degrees
questions.explain: A bell-crank is an L-shaped linkage pivoted at the corner that changes the direction of a force through roughly 90 degrees, as in bicycle brakes.

questions.q: A cam and follower converts...
options: Rotary motion into a change of direction only
questions.explain: As the cam rotates, the follower rises and falls, converting rotary input into reciprocating (up-and-down) output.

questions.q: The part of a cam's rotation where the follower stays still is called the...
questions.explain: A dwell is the section of the cam profile where the follower remains at a constant height and does not move.

questions.q: Which follower type is best for tracking a cam with a steep, detailed profile with least friction?
questions.explain: A roller follower rolls on the cam surface, reducing friction and wear, and follows detailed profiles well compared with flat or knife-edge followers.

questions.q: A driver gear has 15 teeth and the driven gear has 45 teeth. What is the gear ratio (driven : driver)?
questions.explain: Gear ratio = driven teeth / driver teeth = 45 / 15 = 3, giving 3 : 1. The larger driven gear turns three times more slowly.

questions.q: A driver gear with 30 teeth turns at 60 rpm and drives a gear with 15 teeth. What is the output speed?
questions.explain: Output speed = input speed x (driver teeth / driven teeth) = 60 x (30/15) = 120 rpm. The smaller driven gear spins faster.

questions.q: Adding an idler gear between the driver and driven gears will...
options: Convert rotary motion to linear motion
Double the speed of the driven gear
Reverse the direction of the driven gear without changing the ratio
questions.explain: An idler gear changes only the direction of rotation of the driven gear; it does not affect the overall gear ratio.

questions.q: A driver pulley of 40 mm diameter drives a 120 mm pulley by a belt. What is the velocity ratio (driven : driver)?
questions.explain: Velocity ratio = driven diameter / driver diameter = 120 / 40 = 3, i.e. 3 : 1. The larger driven pulley turns three times more slowly.

questions.q: Why is a chain-and-sprocket drive used on a bicycle instead of a belt?
options: It is lighter than any belt
It cannot slip, giving a positive, reliable drive
questions.explain: The chain engages positively with the sprocket teeth so it will not slip under load, unlike a smooth belt-and-pulley drive.

questions.q: A designer wants two pulleys joined by a belt to turn in OPPOSITE directions. How can this be done?
options: Add more tension to the belt
Cross the belt in a figure-of-eight
questions.explain: Crossing the belt (figure-of-eight) makes the driven pulley rotate in the opposite direction to the driver; an open belt gives the same direction.

questions.q: A lever lifts a load of 800 N using an effort of 200 N. What is the mechanical advantage?
questions.explain: Mechanical advantage = load / effort = 800 / 200 = 4. An MA above 1 means a small effort moves a larger load.

questions.q: A mechanism that gives a mechanical advantage greater than 1 allows a user to...
options: Move a larger load using a smaller effort
Increase output speed with no force change
Move a smaller load using a larger effort
questions.explain: When MA is greater than 1 the output (load) force is bigger than the input (effort), so a small effort can move a large load, though over a shorter distance.
